```{r}
# (A. Can you improve this analysis code?
df <- data.frame(a=1:10, b=seq(200,400,length=10),c=11:20,d=NA)
df$a <- (df$a - min(df$a)) / (max(df$a) - min(df$a))
df$b <- (df$b - min(df$a)) / (max(df$b) - min(df$b))
df$c <- (df$c - min(df$c)) / (max(df$c) - min(df$c))
df$d <- (df$d - min(df$d)) / (max(df$a) - min(df$d))
```

```{r}
# Can you improve this analysis code?
library(bio3d)
s1 <- read.pdb("4AKE") # kinase with drug
s2 <- read.pdb("1AKE") # kinase no drug
s3 <- read.pdb("1E4Y") # kinase with drug
s1.chainA <- trim.pdb(s1, chain="A", elety="CA")
s2.chainA <- trim.pdb(s2, chain="A", elety="CA")
s3.chainA <- trim.pdb(s1, chain="A", elety="CA")
s1.b <- s1.chainA$atom$b
s2.b <- s2.chainA$atom$b
s3.b <- s3.chainA$atom$b
plotb3(s1.b, sse=s1.chainA, typ="l", ylab="Bfactor")
plotb3(s2.b, sse=s2.chainA, typ="l", ylab="Bfactor")
plotb3(s3.b, sse=s3.chainA, typ="l", ylab="Bfactor")
```

> **Q6.** How would you generalize the original code above to work with any set of input
protein structures? Write your own function starting from the code above that analyzes protein drug interactions by reading in any protein PDB data and outputs a plot for the specified protein.

```{r}
plot_bf <- function(pdb_id, chain = "A", elety = "CA") {
  pdb <- read.pdb(pdb_id)
  
  #   pdb_id - a 4-character PDB code (e.g. "4AKE") or a path to a PDB file
  #   chain  - which chain to analyze (default "A")
  #   elety  - atom type to keep (default "CA", alpha carbons = one atom per residue)
  
  # Keep only the requested chain and atom type
  chain_atom <- trim.pdb(pdb, chain = chain, elety = elety)
 
  # Extract the B-factor for each residue
  bf <- chain_atom$atom$b

  # Plot B-factors with secondary structure in the margins
  plotb3(bf, sse = chain_atom, typ = "l", ylab = "Bfactor",
         
  # paste() glues words together with spaces.Example, for 1E4Y the title reads “B-factors for 1E4Y chain A” - Please note that I used assistance from AI to add this line to enhance the plots
         
         main = paste("B-factors for", pdb_id, "chain", chain))
}
```

```{r}

# Example: run the function on the three kinase structures

# Type in any of the three kinases
plot_bf("1E4Y")

# Several proteins at once, without repeating the code
ids <- c("4AKE", "1AKE", "1E4Y")

# Loop over each PDB ID and make its B-factor plot
for (id in ids) {
  plot_bf(id)
}
```
